issues.display_title: Issue #189: Duplicate freezes the window and never shows its progress modal
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.14.14.55.mov

What happens

Duplicating a multi-file selection freezes the window for the length of the copy, and the progress modal never appears — the copy itself finishes fine, but the app is unusable while it runs.

Two independent causes:

First, the UI thread. Every file the copy creates fires a watcher add, and each one made useBrowseFileEvents re-sort the entire folder and re-key every entry ({...item, sequence: index}), so every card in the grid re-rendered — once per duplicated file. Duplicating N files is O(N²) work on the renderer's main thread, which is what froze the window; the progress modal's state was being dispatched correctly all along, it just never got a frame to paint in.

Second, the native context menu's Duplicate did nothing at all. on_menu_event called the async msg_duplicate without awaiting or spawning it, so the future was dropped on the spot — no copy, and no duplicate progress events for the renderer's modal either. (The toolbar button never hit this; it goes through the command directly.)

The Rust side was already off the main thread — msg_duplicate runs its copy loop on spawn_blocking and emits duplicate processing/insert/success events per file.

How to reproduce

  1. Open a folder in Browse (Preview or Edit).
  2. Select a few dozen images.
  3. Toolbar → Duplicate (the clone icon).
  4. The window freezes until every copy lands; no progress modal shows.

Context-menu variant: right-click a selection → Duplicate → nothing happens at all.

Goal

Duplicating a large selection keeps the window responsive and shows the progress modal ticking from 0 to N, from both the toolbar and the right-click menu.

  • src-tauri/src/commands/context_menu.rs (on_menu_event) — spawn the msg_duplicate future instead of dropping it, matching the ChangeProjectType arm right below it. Context-menu Duplicate now actually copies and emits its progress events.
  • src/renderer/components/core/ipcHandlers/fileManager.ts (files-watcher) — coalesce a burst of watcher add/addDir entries into one setAddedFile dispatch (120ms window, deduped by path) instead of one dispatch per file. Collapses the O(N²) full-folder re-sort into a single pass per burst, so the UI thread stays free and the modal paints. Covers every bulk-create path — paste, batch export — not just duplicate.

Done on branch fix/loadfolder; pnpm typecheck + cargo check clean.

Follow-up (not in this change)

  • The grid is not virtualized: one re-render still touches every card. Worth doing if folders in the 2k+ range stay heavy after this.
  • One get-file-entry IPC round-trip per created file — batch it if the burst itself becomes the bottleneck.

issues.display_title: Issue #187: Folder with uncached GPS positions blocks navigation until the sweep finishes
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-20.at.15.19.47.mov

Problem

Opening a folder with tens of thousands of panoramas whose GPS positions are not cached yet locks navigation: every way out of the folder — Back/Forward (mouse buttons 4/5), breadcrumbs, the path bar, reload, double-clicking another folder — is guarded by layout.onGettingGPSData and either does nothing or shows the "file is being validated" alert. The user is stuck watching the map spinner until the whole folder has been read, which on a network share is minutes.

Two things make it worse:

  1. The sweep cannot be cancelled. extract-gps-data reads every path in one par_iter pass and only writes to the gps table when the entire folder is done. Leaving the folder (once that were possible) would keep the disk/SMB reads running for a folder nobody is looking at.
  2. No resume. Because the cache write is all-or-nothing, an interrupted sweep leaves nothing behind — re-entering the folder starts from zero. And the renderer treats any cached row as "folder is fully cached" (if (cached.length) { publish; return; }), so a partial cache would be published as if it were complete.

Request

  • Back / navigation must work while the GPS sweep is running.
  • Leaving the folder stops the sweep.
  • Re-entering the folder continues from where it stopped instead of restarting.

Acceptance criteria

  • While GPS extraction runs, Back/Forward, breadcrumbs, path bar, reload and opening another folder all work normally (the onValidating guard stays; only the GPS guard goes).
  • Navigating away cancels the running extraction — no EXIF reads continue for the folder that was left.
  • Partial progress is cached, so re-entering the folder only reads the files that are still missing.
  • A late reply from a cancelled sweep never publishes its markers onto the folder that is open now.
  • The map spinner (DefaultMapCorner) still shows while a sweep is in progress.

Implementation

On development (working tree, not committed yet):

  • src-tauri/src/commands/metadata.rs — extract_gps_data now runs in chunks of 200 files; each chunk is written to the gps table as it lands, and a GPS_GENERATION counter is checked between chunks so a newer folder load stops the sweep. Same pattern as image::PREWARM_GENERATION. Adds cancel_gps_extract().
  • src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs — load-files calls cancel_gps_extract() next to the existing thumbnail prewarm cancel, so every navigation entry point cancels the sweep without a new IPC channel.
  • src/renderer/features/preview/hooks/usePreviewGPSData.ts — diffs the cached rows against the folder's images and asks Rust only for the missing paths (this is the resume), publishes the cached subset immediately, and guards the late reply with the requested directory.
  • Removed the onGettingGPSData guard from the 8 navigation call sites (preview/Browse.tsx, fileManager/Browse.tsx, Edit/Browse.tsx, PathBar.tsx, PanelBreadcrumbs.tsx, MessageModal.tsx, preview/Preview.tsx mouse back/forward). onValidating is untouched.

Not covered

Real progress reporting. The indicator still jumps 0% → 100%; showing per-chunk progress needs a progress event from Rust to the renderer. Worth a follow-up if the spinner looks hung on very large folders.

Unblocked UI Navigation: Previously, navigating out of an uncached folder during a GPS sweep was entirely blocked across 8 navigation entry points by layout.onGettingGPSData (showing "file is being validated" alerts or ignoring input). All navigation guards have been removed, allowing immediate path changes, folder opening, breadcrumb navigation, and back/forward operations.
  2. Instant Cancellation via Generation Counter: Navigating away from a folder immediately triggers cancel_gps_extract() inside commands::files::load_files, incrementing GPS_GENERATION. Rust halts background EXIF reads between 200-file chunks, preventing disk/SMB I/O thrashing for abandoned folders.
  3. Chunked Persistence & Resumable Cache: Extraction runs in chunks of 200 files, committing each chunk to the SQLite gps table as it lands. Re-entering a partially swept folder reads the cached rows immediately and only requests extraction for the missing subset (images.filter(f => !cachedPaths.has(f.path))).

• Immediate Presentation: Publishes already cached coordinates right away while remaining files are read in background.
• Directory Isolation: Compares activeDir !== dir before publishing results to drop late replies from abandoned sweeps.		 ✅ Passed
Navigation Call Sites (8 modules) PathBar.tsx, PanelBreadcrumbs.tsx, Browse.tsx, Preview.tsx • Removed Navigation Lock: Completely removed if (layout.onGettingGPSData) return; guards while preserving onValidating guards for file consistency. ✅ Passed

3. Testing Methodologies & Strategy

  • White-Box Testing:
    • Code review of Rust generation counter pattern (GPS_GENERATION.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst)) and incremental chunk writes.
    • Inspected usePreviewGPSData.ts diffing algorithm and activeDir latch.
  • Gray-Box Testing:
    • Verified SQLite gps table persistence during interrupted sweeps.
    • Inspected Redux state transitions: onGettingGPSData, files.gpsData, and verified markers from folder_a do not contaminate folder_b.
  • Black-Box Testing:
    • Real-device desktop automation on Windows 11 with 60 panoramas in folder_a and 3 panoramas in folder_b.
    • Triggered GPS extraction in Preview on folder_a, immediately navigated to folder_b mid-sweep (measured 4.4s instant navigation without hang), and re-entered folder_a verifying instantaneous cache restoration (4.6s).

issues.display_title: Issue #173: Implement 2D Object Remover in Edit
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

Description

Problem: Getting rid of something you don't want in a photo — a stray bin, a parked car, a person walking through the shot, a sign — means leaving the app entirely and doing it in Photoshop or an online editor. For a photographer working through a folder of listing photos that is a lot of back and forth, and the app can't help with any of it.

Solution: A new Edit tool that removes objects from ordinary flat photos. Mark what you want gone, and AI rebuilds what should be behind it.

How marking works: two ways, and they can be mixed on the same photo.

  • Box — drag a rectangle around the object. Fast, good for something standing on its own.
  • Brush — trace over the object. Slower, but a rectangle drawn around an object in a crowded scene always takes its neighbours with it, and the brush follows the actual shape instead.

Each mark can be given a name ("bin", "car") to tell the AI what it is looking at, and can be reselected, moved, resized or deleted before you run it.

Behavior:

  • The tool only accepts standard flat photos. Dropping a 360° panorama shows a message pointing to the 360 version of this tool instead.
  • Save as new file ON writes the result to an Object remover folder next to the original, leaving the original untouched. OFF replaces the original — with a confirmation prompt first, so nobody overwrites a photo by accident.
  • The result appears in a before/after slider so the change can be judged against the original.
  • Everything outside the marks is kept as it was. Both AI providers re-render the whole frame rather than editing only the marked patch, so furniture, paperwork and table edges nowhere near the target used to come back subtly redrawn — the finished image now takes those pixels from the source photo.
  • Needs an AI API key (added under Preferences). The Remove button stays disabled until a valid key exists, so the failure is visible up front rather than after a long wait.

Shipped in #185.

issues.display_title: Issue #174: Implement 360 Object Remover in Edit
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by developer

2026-08-14.20-09-46.mp4

Problem: The same unwanted-object problem as #173, but for 360° panoramas — and there the usual tools are worse. A panorama opened in a normal photo editor looks stretched and distorted at the top and bottom, the left and right edges have to line up seamlessly or the sphere visibly breaks, and most AI tools hand back something that no longer works as a 360 at all.

Solution: A 360 version of the Object Remover. Same marking, same result, but built so a panorama survives it.

Why it needs its own tool: a panorama can't just be handed to the AI whole — the projection stretches everything near the ceiling and floor, and the seam where the two edges meet gets broken. Instead the app takes each marked object as its own normal-looking view, cleans that view, and merges it back into the sphere. The user doesn't see any of this; they mark and press the button.

How marking works: identical to #173 — box or brush, mixed freely, each mark nameable and editable before running.

Behavior:

  • Only accepts 360° panoramas. Dropping a flat photo points to the 2D version instead.
  • Save as new file ON writes to a 360 Object remover folder next to the original. OFF replaces the original, with a confirmation prompt first.
  • The panorama stays a panorama. The hidden information that marks a file as 360° (which is what makes viewers and Street View show it as a sphere rather than a stretched rectangle) is carried over to the result, along with the camera details and date. Without this the output would silently stop being a usable panorama.
  • Each marked object is handled separately, so if one of them fails the rest still come through. When that happens the app says the result is partial instead of reporting a clean success, so nobody ships a panorama assuming everything was removed.
  • If every object fails, the original file is left completely untouched rather than being replaced by a pointless re-save.
  • Needs an AI API key, same as #173.

issues.display_title: Issue #170: Switching panoramas in Preview freezes the app on network shares
issues.main_description_html:
What happens

Switching between panoramas in Preview on a network share freezes the app. Not on the first switch — it gets worse the longer the session runs, and eventually the window stops responding entirely. Three separate causes stack on the same code path.

1. Prefetch fans out to four neighbours in parallel, with no way to stop it

src/renderer/features/preview/ImageSphere.tsx:42-70 runs on every texture change and prefetches four surrounding files (before, after, prevTop, nextTop). Each one does:

  • getImageUrl(file) → get-image-view + get-image-size
  • useTexture.preload(url) → a full-resolution download over gtimg://

Nothing cancels an in-flight prefetch when the selection moves on. Arrowing through ten images leaves up to ~50 whole-file reads in flight at once. On a local disk this is invisible; on a share it saturates the link, fills the blocking pool, and every one of them holds an entire panorama in memory at the same time (src-tauri/src/lib.rs:190 — Vec::with_capacity(len) + read_to_end, tracked separately in #163).

2. Textures are never disposed

There is no dispose(), useTexture.clear() or THREE.Cache.remove anywhere in the renderer. drei's useTexture caches by URL in a global suspense cache and frees nothing, so every panorama ever displayed stays resident as a decoded bitmap plus a GPU texture. An 8000×4000 equirectangular is ~128 MB of VRAM. The setLoaded([0]) reset on directory change (ImageSphere.tsx:72-76) only resets React state — the cache survives it.

This is why the freeze is intermittent rather than immediate: it needs enough switches to exhaust memory.

3. get-image-size blocks an async-runtime worker

src-tauri/src/commands/files.rs:248 is async fn, but its body is fully blocking sync I/O with no spawn_blocking: imagesize::size, read_orientation and fs::metadata each open the file — three round-trips per file, multiplied by the prefetch fan-out. Same sweep as 5bfa5f1 and #168; this command was missed.

Contributing: the URL cache silently loses entries

src/renderer/hooks/useGetImage.tsx:69-72 writes setLoadedBlobUrl({ ...loadedBlobUrl, [path]: url }), spreading a copy captured in the closure. The displayed panorama and its prefetched neighbours resolve concurrently, so whichever lands last drops the others' entries. The cache keeps missing and the same files are fetched again on the next switch. fileDimensions already has mergeFileDimensions for exactly this reason; loadedBlobUrl never got the equivalent.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount a slow network share (SMB over a VPN/tunnel makes it obvious).
  2. Open a folder of full-resolution equirectangular panoramas from that share in Preview.
  3. Hold the right arrow key, or click through 15–30 panoramas at a normal browsing pace.
  4. The window stalls for progressively longer between images, then stops responding.

Watching memory during step 3 shows it climbing and never coming back down. The stall does not clear by waiting — only by restarting.

Goal

  1. Switching panoramas on a network share stays responsive, and stays responsive for the length of a browsing session rather than degrading.
  2. The number of concurrent full-resolution reads is bounded and does not scale with how fast the user is switching. A prefetch for an image the user has already moved past must not keep running.
  3. Texture memory is bounded. A texture that falls out of the working set is disposed; a texture still bound to the sphere never is (disposing that one renders it black).
  4. Prefetching still earns its keep: stepping to the next or previous image on a slow share should be near-instant, and stepping back to one just visited must not re-download it.
  5. The visible panorama loads before any prefetch starts — a prefetch must never delay the image the user actually asked for.
  6. Existing behaviour is unchanged: the loading overlay in PanoramaViewer.tsx, the progress bar in PanoramaLoader.tsx, the error modal from useViewerImage, and flat/little-planet/video view modes.

End-to-end testing on Windows 11 with a live mapped SMB network share (Z:\Work\qa-nas-test\panoramas_360) confirms that Issue #170 is completely resolved:

  1. Bounded LRU Texture Cache: textureCache.ts implements a 4-entry LRU cache (createTextureCache) that disposes unreferenced textures from VRAM/memory upon eviction, while strictly preserving the active texture currently rendered on the sphere (keep parameter).

issues.display_title: Issue #167: Creating a folder inside a mounted USB or network volume fails
issues.main_description_html:
DEMO FROM DEVELOPER

Screen.Recording.2026-08-07.at.14.59.21.mov

What happens

Creating a new folder inside a mounted USB or network volume fails. On macOS/Linux, create-folder prepends $HOME to the requested path unconditionally:

src-tauri/src/commands/fs_ops.rs — create_folder

let home = dirs::home_dir()...;
format!("{home}/{folder}")

The renderer sends the new folder as a display path, <currentDirectory>/<name> — for a share mounted at /Volumes/sambashare that is sambashare/Panorama/New folder. Prefixing home turns it into $HOME/sambashare/Panorama/New folder, whose parent does not exist, so the non-recursive create_dir fails with NotFound.

This is the same class of bug as #160 (copy/move into a mounted volume). That fix introduced the volumes-aware helper resolve_dest in the same file, but create_folder was never moved over to it — it is the only remaining hardcoded home_dir in fs_ops.rs.

Absolute paths are broken by the same line: /Volumes/x/y becomes $HOME//Volumes/x/y.

How to reproduce

  1. Mount an SMB share (e.g. as /Volumes/sambashare).
  2. In the app, navigate into the share — File Manager panel or Preview both reach this path.
  3. Create a new folder (toolbar button, context menu, or the app menu item).
  4. It fails. Nothing appears in the listing; the folder is not created on the share.

Compare with the same action inside a folder under $HOME, which works — that is the case the $HOME prefix was written for.

Goal

A new folder lands where the user asked, on a mounted volume as well as under home.

The fix is to route through the existing resolve_dest helper, but with one catch worth recording: resolve_dest distinguishes a home-relative display path from a mounted-volume one by testing which candidate exists. The folder being created never exists yet, so passing it the full path always loses that test and falls back to $HOME — the naive fix does not work. The parent has to be resolved, then the new name joined onto it:

let normalized = folder.replace('\\', "/");
let final_path = match normalized.rsplit_once('/') {
    Some((parent, name)) => resolve_dest(parent).join(name),
    None => resolve_dest(&normalized),
};

A fix along these lines, plus a regression test (create_folder_honours_a_path_outside_home, which creates a folder in a temp dir outside $HOME), is prepared on branch fix/nas but not yet committed or pushed. Needs verifying against a real share before it lands.
